runtime: Two Windows 11 workstations (25H2 build 26200 and an Insider build 26340), Entra-joined and Intune-managed; Intune Remediations agent, Windows PowerShell 5.1 64-bit, run as SYSTEM. Node.js MSI 22.17.1 and 22.18.0 installed before the run; target nodejs.org release v22.23.4 (x64 MSI).
procedure: Assigned through Intune Remediations (hourly) to a group containing only the device owner, sent initiateOnDemandProactiveRemediation to both devices, then read deviceRunStates via Microsoft Graph beta and the Defender for Endpoint software evidence (DeviceTvmSoftwareEvidenceBeta) via advanced hunting.
expected: Remediation upgrades Node.js to the newest 22.x MSI after hash and signature checks; post-remediation detection is compliant.
observed: Device 1: pre-detection 'Node.js 22.17.1 is older than 22.23.4.', remediationState success, post-detection 'Node.js 22.23.4 is the latest 22.x.' Device 2: Defender evidence moved from 22.18.0 (2026-11-02) to 22.23.4 (uninstall registry entry, 2026-11-03), latest run 'Node.js 22.23.4 is the latest 22.x.'
limitations: Two devices, x64 only; the ARM64 branch was not exercised.
No device had Node.js running a long-lived process during the upgrade; msiexec returned success without a restart request on the device whose run was captured.

The second device's last reported run is a later compliant detection; its remediation run was not captured in deviceRunStates, but Defender evidence shows the MSI version change from 22.18.0 to 22.23.4.
